text: Rosarno is a comune in the Metropolitan City of Reggio Calabria in the Italian region of Calabria. It is about 70 kilometres (43 mi) southwest of Catanzaro and about 50 kilometres (31 mi) northeast of Reggio Calabria.

text: Pope Benedict XVI was the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of the Vatican City from 2005 until his resignation in 2013. Following his resignation, he chose to be known as "pope emeritus", a title he held until his death on 31 December 2022.

title: Pope Benedict XVI makes a controversial visit to the Great Synagogue of Rome.
text: The Great Synagogue of Rome is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, that is located at Lungotevere de' Cenci, in Rome, in Lazio, Italy. Designed by Vincenzo Costa and Osvaldo Armanni in an eclectic mix of Historicism and Art Nouveau styles, the synagogue was completed in 1904.

text: The Catholic Church in Ireland, or Irish Catholic Church, is part of the worldwide Catholic Church in communion with the Holy See. With approximately 4.3 million members, it is the largest Christian Church in Ireland.

text: The Ariston Theatre is a theatre and cinema in Sanremo, Italy. It is best known as the venue of the annual Sanremo Music Festival, which it has hosted since 1977.

text: Italy participated at the 2010 Winter Olympics in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

text: The Diocese of Verona is a Latin diocese of the Catholic Church in northern Italy. The diocese belongs to the Episcopal Conference of Italy, in the Ecclesiastical Province of Venice.

title: At a Palm Sunday mass in Saint Peter's Square, Rome, Pope Benedict XVI tells tens of thousands of people about the recent "petty gossip" he has been subjected to, thought to mean the child sexual abuse within the Roman Catholic Church,…
text: Palm Sunday is the Christian moveable feast that falls on the Sunday before Easter. The feast commemorates Jesus Christ's triumphal entry into Jerusalem, as described in all four canonical Gospels, and takes its name from the palm branches waved by the crowd to greet and honor Jesus as he entered the city.

title: 2010 Italian regional elections.
text: The Italian regional elections of 2010 took place on 28–29 March in 13 regions, including nine of the ten largest ones: Lombardy, Campania, Veneto, Lazio, Piedmont, Emilia-Romagna, Apulia, Tuscany and Calabria.

title: The AppsBuilder project is initiated by Daniele Pelleri and Luigi Giglio in Milan.
text: AppsBuilder was an Italian cloud-based self-service app creator designed to provide users with no coding skills access to tools to build native applications and HTML5 web apps.

title: Murder of Sarah Scazzi.
text: The murder of Sarah Scazzi, also known as the Delitto di Avetrana was a murder which occurred on 26 August 2010, in Avetrana, in the province of Taranto, Italy. Fifteen-year-old Sarah Scazzi was strangled by her cousin Sabrina Misseri and her aunt Cosima Serrano, who then hid the body together with her father Michele Misseri, staging a kidnapping by a third party.

title: Fernando Alonso wins the Italian Grand Prix. This would be Ferrari's last win at Monza until 2019.
text: Fernando Alonso Díaz is a Spanish racing driver who competes in Formula One for Aston Martin. Alonso has won two Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles, which he won in 2005 and 2006 with Renault, and has won 32 Grands Prix across 23 seasons.

title: “Bad Romance” by Lady Gaga
text: "Bad Romance" is a song by American singer-songwriter Lady Gaga from her third extended play, The Fame Monster (2009)—the reissue of her debut studio album, The Fame (2008). Following an unauthorized demo leak, Gaga premiered the final version of the song during Alexander McQueen's 2010 Paris Fashion Week show in October 2009.

title: “Baciami ancora” by 11 January
text: "Baciami ancora" is a song by Italian singer-songwriter Jovanotti. It was released on 8 January 2010 through Universal Music Italy for the soundtrack of the Italian film Kiss Me Again directed by Gabriele Muccino.

title: “Per tutta la vita” by Noemi
text: "Per tutta la vita" is a song recorded by Italian singer Noemi. It was released on 17 February 2010 as the lead single from the deluxe edition of the singer's debut studio album Sulla mia pelle.

title: “Per tutte le volte che...” by 22 February
text: "Per tutte le volte che..." is a 2010 song written by Pierdavide Carone and performed by Valerio Scanu. It won the 60th edition of the Sanremo Music Festival.
listen: Per tutte le volte che... 22 February

title: “Each Tear” by Mary J. Blige featuring Tiziano Ferro
text: "Each Tear" is a song performed by American R&B recording artist Mary J. Blige. It was released as the second international single from her ninth studio album, Stronger with Each Tear.
listen: Each Tear Mary J. Blige featuring Tiziano Ferro

title: “Un colpo all'anima” by Ligabue
text: Luciano Riccardo Ligabue, commonly known as Ligabue or Liga, is an Italian singer-songwriter, film director, and writer.

title: “Alors on danse” by 3 May
text: "Alors on danse" is a song by Belgian singer Stromae. It was released in September 2009 in Belgium and in February 2010 in the rest of Europe.

title: “Quello che dai” by Marco Carta
text: Marco Carta is an Italian singer. To date, he has sold more than 245,000 albums and 60,000 singles.

title: “Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)” by 17 May
text: "Waka Waka" is a song by Colombian singer Shakira, featuring the South African band Freshlyground. Co-written by Shakira and John Hill, it was released on 7 May 2010 by Epic Records as the official song of the 2010 FIFA World Cup, which was held in South Africa.
listen: Waka Waka (This Time for Africa) 17 May

title: “Love the Way You Lie” by Eminem featuring Rihanna
text: "Love the Way You Lie" is a song by American rapper Eminem featuring Barbadian singer Rihanna from Eminem's seventh studio album Recovery. Skylar Grey wrote and recorded a demo of the song alongside producer Alex da Kid.
listen: Love the Way You Lie Eminem featuring Rihanna

title: “White Knuckle Ride” by Jamiroquai
text: "White Knuckle Ride" is the first single from British funk/acid jazz group Jamiroquai's studio album Rock Dust Light Star. The single was released via Digital Download on 31 October 2010, with a Limited Edition Vinyl release due to appear on 1 January 2011.

title: “Loca” by Shakira featuring Dizzee Rascal
text: "Loca" is a song by Colombian singer-songwriter Shakira and the lead single from her ninth studio album, Sale el Sol (2010). It was based on a previously-released version by Dominican rapper El Cata, and two versions were released.

title: “Only Girl (In the World)” by 8 November
text: "Only Girl" is a song by Barbadian singer Rihanna from her fifth studio album, Loud (2010). It was released as the album's lead single on September 10, 2010, by Def Jam Recordings.

title: “The Time (Dirty Bit)” by The Black Eyed Peas
text: "The Time" is a song by American musical group the Black Eyed Peas from their sixth studio album, The Beginning. It was written by group members will.i.am and apl.de.ap along with DJ Ammo, who produced the song with will.i.am.
listen: The Time (Dirty Bit) The Black Eyed Peas

title: “In punta di piedi” by 22 November
text: "In punta di piedi" is the debut single by Nathalie, an Italian singer-songwriter of mixed Tunisian-Belgian origins who won the fourth season of Italian series of The X Factor on 2010. Written by Nathalie herself, the song was her winner's single.

title: “Tutto l'amore che ho” by Jovanotti
text: "Tutto l'amore che ho" is a song by Italian singer-songwriter Jovanotti. It was released on 3 December 2010 through Universal Music Italy as the lead single from his twelfth studio album Ora.
